The paper asserts, as following 'easily from Proposition 6.2 of [76], now applied to twists of a modular curve', that there exist a second elliptic curve A, a number field L/K and primes p and q such that: (1) the mod-p representation r̄ = (Sym^{2n−1} ρ̄_{E,p})|G_L, with its p-adic lift, satisfies all the hypotheses of Theorem 5.16 except possibly residual modularity; (2) A and E are semistable over L and have good reduction at all primes dividing p and q; (3) p and q split completely in L; (4) q + 1 [printed p + 1] is divisible by an integer N_2 > 2n + 1 [printed N_2 > n + 1] prime to the conductor of A; (5) E[p] ≃ A[p] [printed E[q] ≃ A[q]] as G_L-modules, and the corresponding mod-p representation G_L → GL_2(F_p) is surjective; (6) the mod-q representation [printed mod-p] ρ̄_A : G_L → GL_2(F_q) is surjective, and ρ̄_A|G_{L_w} ≃ Ind_{G_{Q_{q²}}}^{G_{Q_q}} ω_2 for each place w | q of L. This is the relabelling recorded in sourceIssues E215, E216.
items.note: The paper derives it from [76, Proposition 6.2] applied to twists of a modular curve, i.e. Moret–Bailly (R23.1, planned) on the twisted modular curve parametrizing A with A[q] ≅ E[q] and the local conditions at p. The rank-two twisted moduli step is planned only for Hilbert–Blumenthal moduli (R23.2), not for twisted modular curves over an arbitrary K. Clause (1) refers to the conditional Theorem 5.16. The printed 'mod-p' in (1) and (5) should read mod-q. See sourceIssues E213 (bound should be N_2 > 2n + 1) and E215, E216 (inconsistent roles of p and q). Review (REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18): the bound is N₂ > 2n + 1: BLGHT II Theorem 6.4 has 'N₂ > n + 1' with n the dimension, which is 2n here (checked by the review against BLGHT II, Theorem 6.4 and §4). Review (REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18): the item now uses the relabelling of E216 (keep (1) and the final step at p; change (4), (5), (6)), so items and issues agree; the bound is N₂ > 2n + 1 (E213).

items.name: Potential modularity of Sym^{2n−1}(E) in general
items.statement: Assume Conjecture B. Let E/K be a non-CM elliptic curve and n ≥ 1, and choose (A, L, p, q) as in sec10-auxiliary-curve-lemma. By sec10-special-case for A at q, Sym^{2n−1}(A) is potentially modular over some extension L′/L unramified at p; since E[p] ≃ A[p], Theorem 5.16 applied at p to (Sym^{2n−1} ρ_{E,p})|G_{L′} shows that Sym^{2n−1}(E) is modular over L′, i.e. potentially modular (printed: 'is modular'). The printed text is consistent with this reading once (4)–(6) of the auxiliary lemma are relabelled as in sourceIssues E216.
items.note: This is the p–q switch: from potential modularity of Sym^{2n−1}(A) and E[q] ≅ A[q], it applies Theorem 5.16 at q. It is conditional on Conjecture B and planned nowhere. The published text swaps p and q (sourceIssues E216), and the item records the corrections. Its final 'is modular' means modular over L′, i.e. potentially modular. Review (REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18): aligned with the E216 relabelling, as for sec10-auxiliary-curve-lemma.

items.name: Greenberg–Wiles (Poitou–Tate) Selmer group Euler characteristic formula
items.statement: Let F be a number field, p odd, and S a finite set of places of F containing all places above p and ∞. Let M be a finite G_{F,S}-module of p-power order with Cartier dual M* = Hom(M, μ_{p^∞}). For each v ∈ S let L_v ⊂ H^1(F_v, M) be a subgroup, and let L_v^⊥ ⊂ H^1(F_v, M*) be its annihilator under local Tate duality. Put H^1_L(F, M) = ker(H^1(G_{F,S}, M) → ⊕_{v∈S} H^1(F_v, M)/L_v), and define H^1_{L^⊥}(F, M*) likewise. Then |H^1_L(F, M)| / |H^1_{L^⊥}(F, M*)| = (|H^0(F, M)| / |H^0(F, M*)|) · ∏_{v∈S} |L_v| / |H^0(F_v, M)|.
items.locator: §8.2, p. 402 (displayed formula, with M = F_p); also Prop 8.4(2), p. 410 ('Poitou–Tate duality and the global Euler characteristic formula')
items.note: Planned at ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.5, on top of R02.3 (Tate's global Euler characteristic) and R02.4 (Poitou–Tate). The reviewed library audit lists this exact target as absent. Neither library has G_{F,S}, Galois-cohomological Selmer groups, global Euler characteristics or Poitou–Tate duality. External input: Standard (Wiles 1995 Prop. 1.6; e.g. Darmon–Diamond–Taylor, 'Fermat's Last Theorem', Thm 2.19). The paper cites no reference for it in §8.2; for Prop 8.4(2) it points to the proof of [52, Prop 3.2.5].

items.name: Top-degree cohomology commutes with base change
items.statement: Let P be a complex of S-modules with P^i = 0 for i > l0. Then for every S-module B, H^{l0}(P ⊗_S B) = H^{l0}(P) ⊗_S B, since H^{l0}(P) = coker(P^{l0−1} → P^{l0}) and ⊗ is right exact. The paper uses this implicitly in two places: for 'ψ then gives rise to an isomorphism … between H^{l0}(P^□ ⊗ S∞^□/(a + ϖ^{n′})) and H/ϖ^{n′}H for each N ≥ n′ ≥ 1' (p. 387), and for 'H^{l0}(P∞^□)/a = H^{l0}(P∞^□/a)' (p. 388).
items.note: Keep this as an implicitly used standard lemma, like ext-depth-dim-finite-map and mumford-lemma-2. No existing item states it. Both uses check out on the rendered pages. p. 387 (PDF 91): '(Note that ψ then gives rise to an isomorphism of R∞-modules between H^{l0}(P^□ ⊗_{S∞^□} S∞^□/(a + ϖ^{n′})) and H/ϖ^{n′}H for each N ≥ n′ ≥ 1)'. p. 388 (PDF 92): 'ψ∞ … H^{l0}(P∞^□)/a = H^{l0}(P∞^□/a) ≅ H'. Theorem 6.4's proof (p. 389) uses the same identification. In both cases P^{l0+1} = 0, and P has projective terms, so P ⊗ B also computes the derived tensor product. The lemma is a direct application of Mathlib declarations, all read at the pinned commit. (1) CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesLeftHomology_of_zero_g (Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/ShortComplex/PreservesHomology.lean:886): a functor that preserves the cokernel of S.f preserves the homology of a short complex S with S.g = 0. (2) CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso (same file, :455) gives (S.map F).homology ≅ F.obj S.homology. (3) Base change F = ModuleCat.extendScalars is a left adjoint: ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj (Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/ChangeOfRings.lean:885), with an IsLeftAdjoint instance at :925. So F preserves colimits by CategoryTheory.Adjunction.leftAdjoint_preservesColimits (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Limits.lean:90). (4) At module level, rTensor_exact and rTensor.equiv (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/RightExactness.lean:399, 393) give the cokernel form directly. No single declaration states 'H^{top}(P ⊗ B) = H^{top}(P) ⊗ B', but the lemma is a one-step instance of (1)–(3), with S = P.sc l0, whose g is zero because P^{l0+1} = 0. The derived version (the edge of the Tor spectral sequence) is also in the scope of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7: 'Prove the spectral sequence Tor_i^A(H^j(C),B) ⇒ H^(j−i)(C⊗ᴸ_A B)'.

items.name: Admissible and locally admissible smooth representations over A
items.statement: Let A = O/ϖ^a and G = GL_n(F_x). A smooth representation M of G on an A-module (every vector fixed by an open subgroup) is admissible if M^K is a finitely generated A-module for every compact open subgroup K ⊂ G. It is locally admissible if every v ∈ M lies in an admissible G-subrepresentation of M, equivalently if the G-subrepresentation generated by v is admissible. The category 𝒞 of Definition 9.11 consists of locally admissible modules, and M_j[m] in §9.4.2 is called admissible.
items.note: Checked on pp. 420 and 424 (PDF pp. 124, 128). Definition 9.11 reads 'the category of locally admissible G-modules over A := O/ϖ^k', and §9.4.2 says M_j is filtered 'by the admissible module M_j[m]'. Neither notion is defined in the paper, so the item is kept: it is a definition 𝒞 depends on. Existing items record it only in def-9-11-category-C's xnote ('Locally admissible: every vector generates an admissible subrepresentation'). The equivalence of the item's two formulations uses that A = O/ϖ^a is noetherian, so that a subrepresentation of an admissible representation is admissible. Atlas: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.0 plans admissibility, 'Define admissibility by finite generation of every compact-open invariant module, with stronger finiteness conditions explicitly separated', over the README's 'commutative coefficient rings A', and plans 'closure under subobjects'. Local admissibility is a weaker condition and is named nowhere: a grep for 'locally admissible' over data/atlas.json, research/blueprint/roadmaps and data/decompositions finds nothing. So the item as a whole is not planned. Libraries: there is no admissible or smooth-representation category. Near miss: Tau Ceti TauCeti.IsSmoothDiscrete (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/SmoothDiscrete.lean:254), smoothness (open stabilizers) of a discrete TopRep, with no admissibility.

items.name: Normalized parabolic induction n-ind_B^G and parabolic restriction res_G^B
items.statement: Let B = D·N be the Borel subgroup of G = GL_n(F_x), with unipotent radical N. For a smooth A-representation σ of B trivial on N, n-ind_B^G(σ) is the space of locally constant f : G → σ with f(bg) = δ_B(b)^{1/2} σ(b) f(g), with G acting by right translation. The square root of δ_B exists since √N(x) ∈ Z_p, as N(x) ≡ 1 mod p and p > n ≥ 2. The parabolic restriction res_G^B(M) is the normalized Jacquet module M_N ⊗ δ_B^{−1/2}. It is exact and left adjoint to n-ind_B^G (Frobenius reciprocity Hom_G(M, n-ind_B^G σ) = Hom_B(res_G^B M, σ)), which gives the natural map M → n-ind_B^G res_G^B(M) of Lemma 9.12. For π = n-ind_B^G(χ) as in Lemma 9.9, res_G^B(π) has as constituents the n! distinct characters χ^w, w ∈ W.
items.locator: §9.4.1, Lemmas 9.9 and 9.12, Corollary 9.13, Theorem 9.16, pp. 420–423 (used without definition)
items.note: Checked on pp. 420–423 (PDF pp. 124–127). n-ind_B^G and res_G^B are used in Lemma 9.9, Lemma 9.12 (the natural map M → n-ind_B^G res_G^B(M) and the decomposition res_G^B(M) ≃ ⊕_W M_B^w), Corollary 9.13 and the proof of Theorem 9.16, without definition. They are genuine definitions the section depends on, and no existing item defines them (lem-9-12's note only names SR.2 as the source of tools). Kept. Planned: SR.2 says 'Prove Frobenius reciprocity with correct adjoint direction and hypotheses, induction in stages and Mackey filtrations. For P=MN define unnormalized induction and N-coinvariants, then normalized induction/Jacquet functors using a specified square root of the modulus character. Prove exactness in the valid coefficient regime … and the geometric lemma with double-coset indexing.' The roadmap README says 'Basic categorical constructions use commutative coefficient rings A'. Here A = O/ϖ^a with ℓ ≠ p, so ℓ is a unit in A and N-coinvariants are exact: this is the valid regime. The geometric lemma plus distinctness of the eigenvalues gives the n! distinct constituents χ^w of res_G^B(π). The item's remark that √N(x) ∈ Z_p (N(x) ≡ 1 mod p, p odd, Hensel) is editorial, not in the paper. SR.2's 'specified square root' covers it. Library near misses only: Tau Ceti TauCeti.coind (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Coinduced.lean:82), the unnormalized smooth coinduction {f locally constant, f(ug) = u·f(g)} with right translation; Mathlib ContRepresentation.coind (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Continuous/Basic.lean:547), continuous functions without smoothness or normalization. Neither library has a Jacquet functor or normalized induction.

items.name: Supercuspidal support (mod p, ℓ ≠ p)
items.statement: Let π be an irreducible smooth representation of GL_n(F_x) over F̄_p, where the residue characteristic ℓ of x differs from p. Its supercuspidal support is the multiset {σ_1, …, σ_r} of irreducible supercuspidal representations σ_i of GL_{n_i}(F_x), with Σ n_i = n, such that π is a subquotient of the parabolic induction of σ_1 ⊗ … ⊗ σ_r. It is unique up to permutation (Vignéras). For π = n-ind_B^G(χ) with χ = (χ_1, …, χ_n) it is {χ_1, …, χ_n}.
items.locator: §9.4.1, proof of Lemma 9.10, p. 420 (used without definition)
items.note: Checked on p. 420 (PDF p. 124). The proof of Lemma 9.10 reads: 'The supercuspidal support of π consists of the distinct characters χ_i. If either extension group is non-zero, then, by Theorem 3.2.13 of [80], it follows that π′ has the same supercuspidal support as π.' The notion is used without definition, and no item defines it: emerton-helm-3-2-13 and lem-9-10 use it. Kept as a definition. Atlas: SR.3 plans 'the subquotient description by supercuspidal support' only under 'Admissible complex representations'. The SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups README says: 'Complex Bernstein theory, integral ℓ-adic theory (ℓ≠p) and characteristic-p smooth theory have separate theorem hypotheses. No transfer of admissibility or semisimplicity between them is implicit.' SR.5 (Helm's integral families) plans no mod-ℓ supercuspidal support. So the F̄_p-coefficient notion (ℓ ≠ p) and its uniqueness are not planned. The uniqueness attribution to Vignéras is standard for GL_n but I did not re-check it against the source. Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

items.name: Splitting over a finite-index subgroup implies splitting (characteristic 0)
items.statement: Let L/F be finite Galois with L ⊂ F_S, and H = G_{L,S}, acting trivially on V (the paper chooses L so, p. 367: 'a finite extension L/F such that G_{L,S} acts trivially on V'). If an extension 0 → V → W → V → 0 of continuous E[G_{F,S}]-modules (E of characteristic 0) splits over H, then it splits over G_{F,S}: by inflation–restriction the kernel of H¹(G_{F,S}, End_E V) → H¹(H, End_E V) is H¹(Gal(L/F), (End_E V)^H) = H¹(Gal(L/F), End_E V) = 0.
items.note:
Kept. This is the fourth input of Lemma 4.14, alongside the itemised mazur-def-ring-noetherian, mazur-traces-generate and cft-no-Zp-extension-unramified-at-p. The xnote of lem-4-14-reducedness mentions it but no item states it. Printed on p. 368 (checked on the image, PDF p. 72; arXiv v2 has the same wording): 'because G_{L,S} has finite image in G_{F,S}, the extension also splits over G_{F,S}, because the inflation map is injective (the kernel is computed by H^1 of a finite group acting in characteristic zero)'. The intended meaning is finite index and restriction, not inflation; this is recorded as sourceIssues E99 and E100.
Library, read at the pin: Tau Ceti has continuous H¹ for any topological group G and topological coefficients M. It has restriction explicitRes1 (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/ExplicitFunctoriality.lean:497). It has explicitCor1_comp_res1 (Corestriction.lean:496), 'cor¹ ∘ res¹ = (G : U) • id' on H¹(G, M) for open U of finite index. It has explicitInfRes_exact (Inflation.lean:336), range(infl) = ker(res) in degree 1.
Consequence: ker(res) is killed by the index. For M = End_E V, a Q_p-vector space, H¹ is torsion-free (if n·c = d0(m) then c = d0(m/n)), so res is injective. This is a few-line corollary, not a single declaration.
In the paper's situation, G_{L,S} acts trivially on V, and so also on W once the extension splits over it. The conclusion is then Maschke for the finite group Gal(L/F) over E (char 0): Mathlib MonoidAlgebra.Submodule.exists_isCompl (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Maschke.lean:162, hypotheses [Finite G] [NeZero (Nat.card G : k)]). This route avoids the extension ↔ H¹(G, End V) dictionary, which neither library has. Review (REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18): inflation–restriction gives H¹(Gal(L/F), (End_E V)^H); it equals the printed form because H acts trivially on V, which is now a hypothesis, as in the paper.

items.name: Modular of weight one; finite image (Deligne–Serre)
items.statement: ρ : G_Q → GL₂(O) is modular of weight one if ρ ⊗ K̄ ≅ ρ_f for a classical weight-one cuspidal eigenform f. Such ρ_f (Deligne–Serre) have finite image; so a deformation shown to be modular of weight one has finite image.
items.locator: §1, Corollary 1.5 and the following paragraph, p. 304
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18. R19.1 plans 'the weight-one Artin representation in the Deligne–Serre setting' and R15.5 the Deligne–Serre lifting lemma. Used in Corollaries 1.5–1.6.

items.name: Deduction of Theorem 1.2 from Theorem 1.3
items.statement: For ρ as in Theorem 1.2, semistability makes each ρ̄|I_x unipotent (type S), so hypothesis (4) of Theorem 1.3 holds and ρ is an O-point of R^min. Then R^min ≅ T_m and the freeness of H₁(Y₀(N), O)_m give a characteristic-zero non-Eisenstein eigenclass, hence a cuspidal π with L(ρ, s) = L(π, s).
items.locator: §1, p. 302 ('We deduce Theorem 1.2 from the following more general result')
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18. The paper's own deduction, left implicit.

items.name: Dévissage and cofiniteness for K/O coefficients on curves over O
items.statement: For a vector bundle L on a flat proper O-curve Y (Y = X_Δ(Q), X_Δ(Q; x)): 0 → L_k → L_{K/O} →(ϖ) L_{K/O} → 0 is exact; H⁰(Y, L_{K/O})[ϖ] = H⁰(Y, L_k); and H^i(Y, L_{K/O}) is cofinitely generated over O. Hence End_O H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{K/O}) is O-finite and H_i(Y, L) is finitely generated over O.
items.locator: §3.2, pp. 317 ('T^an is a finite O-algebra'), 320, 322 (proof of Lemma 3.7(1)) and 324
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18. Implicit and standard; E26's repair uses it. Coherent cohomology and base change of proper flat O-schemes is AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension (route 18).

items.name: Cartesian degeneracy squares at Taylor–Wiles level
items.statement: For j = 1, 2, X_Δ(Q; x) ≅ X_Δ(Q) ×_{X₀(Q), π_j} X₀(Q; x), both for x ∤ pNQ and for x | Q: both sides are Δ-torsors over X₀(Q; x) and the map is Δ-equivariant. So the functoriality of Hochschild–Serre makes its differentials T_x- and U_x-equivariant.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18. The paper's own, implicit.

items.name: Kodaira–Spencer and isogenies (Edixhoven, Lemma 7.4)
items.statement: Under Kodaira–Spencer, φ₁₂^{⊗2} = x·(π₂^*Ω¹(∞) → Ω¹_{X_Δ(Q;x)}(∞) ← π₁^*Ω¹(∞)). Hence the Serre adjoint of T_x on H¹(ω^{2−n}(−∞)) is x^{1−n}⟨x⟩^{−1}T_x on H⁰(ω^n).
items.locator: §3.2.4, proof of the Φ-duality, p. 323 (citing [31], inside the proof of Prop. 7.3)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18. Imported from Edixhoven [31]; the key input to Phi-duality-twisted-hecke, whose twisted duality route 6 already sends to R15.3.

items.name: q-expansion principle with torsion coefficients
items.statement: For k ≥ 1 and A = O/ϖ^m or K/O, q-expansion at ∞ gives an injection H⁰(X₁(Q), ω^k_A) ↪ A⟦q⟧, compatible with the usual formulas for T_ℓ, U_x and ⟨a⟩; in weight n with p^{n−1} ≡ 0 mod ϖ^m, U_p acts as U.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18. R15.2 plans 'the q-expansion principle … its integral version'. It gives the vertical maps of the p. 327 diagram, ψ = (φ, ⟨p⟩V_p), the injectivity of ψ and the U_p matrix.

items.name: Theorem 3.30, step (4): reduction to the component at ∞
items.statement: The group ∏_{x∈T(ρ̄)} GL₂(Z_x) acts on X_{V₁(Q)} and on its cohomology, permutes its connected components transitively (through det; π₀ ≅ ∏_{T(ρ̄)} (Z/x^{c_x/2})^×) and commutes with the Hecke operators at p. Hence the q-expansion identities φ∘T_p − U_p∘φ = ⟨p⟩V_p and θV_p = 0 of §§3.3–3.7 hold at level V₁(Q).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18. The paper's own step.

items.name: Theorem 3.30, step (4): the Hasse subquotient with L_σ
items.statement: For n ≫ 0, multiplication by a high power of a Hasse lift realises H⁰(X_{U₁(Q)}, (ω ⊗ L_σ)_{O/ϖ^m})_m as a Hecke-equivariant subquotient of (H⁰(X_{V₁(Q)}, ω^n)_m ⊗ W_σ)^G, using Corollary 3.29.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18. The paper's own step, built on hasse-multiplication-phi and cor-3-29-L-sigma.

items.name: When R_{v,φ} (v ≠ p) is not formally smooth
items.statement: For p odd, v ≠ p and ρ̄|G_v minimal among its twists (after extending k), H²(G_v, ad⁰ρ̄) ≠ 0, i.e. R_{v,φ} is not formally smooth, exactly in four cases: (1) v ≡ 1 mod p, ρ̄|G_v ≅ (unramified) ⊗ (χ ⊕ 1) with χ ramified; (2) v ≡ −1 mod p, ρ̄|G_v absolutely irreducible and induced from Q_{v²}; (3) v ≡ 1 mod p, ρ̄|G_v ≅ (unramified) ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 1) with ∗ ramified; (4) v ≡ −1 mod p, ρ̄|G_v ≅ (unramified) ⊗ (ω̄ ∗; 0 1) with ∗ ramified. The paper lists (1)–(3) (sourceIssues E89).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18. The paper's own classification, via h² = h⁰(ad⁰ρ̄(1)); checked case by case by the review (checker K6).

items.name: Dual Selmer change at Taylor–Wiles primes over an imaginary quadratic field
items.statement: For x ∈ Q with N(x) ≡ 1 mod p and ρ̄(Frob_x) with distinct eigenvalues, 0 → H¹_Q(F, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) → H¹_∅(F, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) → ⊕_{x∈Q} H¹(G_x/I_x, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) is exact, each term H¹(G_x/I_x, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) being one-dimensional, ≅ ad⁰ρ̄/(ρ̄(Frob_x) − 1)ad⁰ρ̄ via [γ] ↦ γ(Frob_x). So a set satisfying Proposition 5.2(2)–(4) has at least q elements and contains one of exactly q.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18. R02.5 plans comparing 'changes of one local condition or addition of a prime', R04.5 'the required dual-Selmer dimension reduction'.

items.name: Serre modular of minimal level (GL_n over F)
items.statement: r̄ : G_F → GL_n(k) is Serre modular of minimal level N(r̄) (the prime-to-p Artin conductor) if some maximal ideal m of the trivial-weight Hecke algebra T_∅ at level N(r̄) has r̄_m ≅ r̄, with r̄_m supplied by Conjecture B.
items.locator: Theorem 5.16(8)(b), p. 384, and the remark there ('only a statement about the existence of a mod-p cohomology class of level N(r̄)'); used in §9.5, p. 425
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18. The paper's own notion, never formally defined; conductor-N-rhobar covers only the imaginary-quadratic GL₂ case.

items.name: Regular algebraic cuspidal π with trivial infinitesimal character
items.statement: A cuspidal π of GL_n(A_F) that is regular algebraic with trivial infinitesimal character at every v | ∞ and unramified at every v | p. Theorem 5.16(8)(a) also presupposes a p-adic Galois representation r_p(π₀) with reduction r̄_p(π₀); for an arbitrary number field F its existence is part of the hypothesis (compare Conjecture B).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18. AG2.0 plans 'Define regular algebraic … cases'. Needed to state Theorem 5.16.

items.name: Borel–Serre compactification of Y(K) and its boundary
items.statement: For K ⊂ G(A^∞) compact open, the Borel–Serre compactification Ȳ(K) is a compact orbifold with corners containing Y(K) as a homotopy-equivalent interior, with boundary ∂Y(K); O(ψ) extends to it, defining H^i_ψ(∂Y_1(Q), O/ϖ^m), which sits in the triangle RΓ_c → RΓ → RΓ_∂.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18. ALS.2 plans 'Borel–Serre compactification … compactness of the quotient and the homotopy equivalence from the interior', ALS.4 the boundary triangle. B(4)(b) is a hypothesis of Theorem 9.19.

items.name: Parahoric invariants of n-ind_B^G M_B (the content of Theorem 9.16)
items.statement: Let M = n-ind_B^G M_B with χ̃ a finite deformation of χ. Then M^{G(O_x)} ≅ (M_B)^{D(O_x)}, and M^{U_0(x)} ≅ ⊕_{m=1}^n (χ̃(m) ⊗ n-ind(χ̃(m̂)))^{L(O_x)} ≅ ⊕_{m=1}^n (M_B)^{D(O_x)}. V acts on the m-th summand by χ̃(m)(ϖ_x), and the normalized sum of the summands is the image of M^{G(O_x)}; hence e_α maps that image isomorphically onto the summand with α_m = α.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18. The paper's own computation; SR.2's geometric lemma and RG2.4's Iwahori–Bruhat decomposition are tools only.

items.name: The twisted modular curve X_E(q)
items.statement: For E/L and a prime q ≥ 3, the curve X_E(q)/L parametrizing elliptic curves A with a Weil-pairing-compatible isomorphism A[q] ≅ E[q]; it is smooth and geometrically connected, and it is the variety fed to Moret-Bailly in §10.
items.locator: §10, p. 429 ('Proposition 6.2 of [76], now applied to twists of a modular curve')
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18. Imported; R23.2 plans Hilbert–Blumenthal moduli only.

items.name: Ext between distinct characters of the torus
items.statement: Distinct smooth characters of D(F_x) = (F_x^×)^n over A have vanishing Ext^i for all i; hence the block splitting res(M) = ⊕_W M_B^w.
items.locator: §9.4.1, proof of Lemma 9.12, p. 420 ('Ext^i(χ^v, χ^w) = 0 for all i if v ≠ w')
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18. The paper's own, standard.

routes.title: GL₂ Modularity Lifting, Part II: minimal R = T in defect one for weight-one forms over Q and Bianchi forms
routes.brief:
GL₂ Modularity Lifting (GL2ModularityLifting) proves modularity lifting for residually modular GL₂ representations over totally real fields. It follows KW II: defect ℓ₀ = 0, Hecke modules concentrated in one degree, and Wiles's numerical coincidence. It has no layer for defect ℓ₀ = 1, where the Hecke modules are not flat over O and the automorphic forms contribute to two degrees of cohomology. It also has no layer for weight-one coherent cohomology or for Bianchi manifolds. This Part II starts there. It follows Part 1 of Calegari–Geraghty, "Modularity lifting beyond the Taylor–Wiles method", Invent. Math. 211 (2018) 297–433 (§§1, 3, 4.1 and 5; arXiv:1207.4224v2), and proves minimal R = T when ℓ₀ = 1. Its engine is Proposition 2.3: patching balanced modules over S_N = O[(Z/p^N)^q], with q − 1 variables in R∞. That proposition is already planned, with its proof, in DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.5 (the reviewed node balanced-modules-and-module-patching, whose source is this paper).

Final theorems, as the paper states them, with the corrections recorded in sourceIssues:
- Theorem 1.4 (proved as Theorem 3.30, p. 350, and Theorem 3.26, p. 339, when there are no vexing primes). Let p ≥ 3 and let ρ̄: G_Q → GL₂(k) be odd, continuous and irreducible, of Serre level N and unramified at p. Then there are a quotient X_U of X₁(N) and a vector bundle L_σ on X_U such that R^min ≅ T_m, where T is the Hecke algebra of H¹(X_U, ω ⊗ L_σ), and H¹(X_U, ω ⊗ L_σ)_m is free over T_m. The theorem needs the standing hypothesis of §3.1 that ρ̄^{I_x} ≠ 0 when ρ̄|G_x is reducible, up to twist.
- Corollary 1.5, with its minimality hypothesis made explicit, and Corollary 1.6. A minimal deformation of such a ρ̄ unramified at p is modular of weight one, and has finite image over any A in C_O.
- Theorem 3.11: local–global compatibility for Katz forms of weight one over O/ϖ^m. For Q a set of Taylor–Wiles primes, there is a deformation ρ_Q: G_Q → GL₂(T_m) of ρ̄, unramified outside NQ (in particular at p), with traces T_x. Its twist is minimal outside Q and has the stated shape at x | Q. The proof uses the Hasse invariant and the doubling map ψ = (φ, φ∘T_p − U_p∘φ), and runs in three cases: distinct eigenvalues; α = β non-scalar, via Wiese's Lemma 3.17; and ρ̄(Frob_p) scalar, via J = I for the local ring R̃†.
- Theorem 4.8 (multiplicity one or two). If ρ̄ is ramified at p, or unramified at p with ρ̄(Frob_p) non-scalar, then J₁(N*)[m] ≅ ρ̄. If it is unramified with ρ̄(Frob_p) scalar, then J₁(N*)[m] ≅ ρ̄ ⊕ ρ̄.
- Theorem 5.11 and Theorems 1.2 and 1.3. F is imaginary quadratic, p ≥ 3 is unramified in F, and Conjecture A is assumed for all Q. If m∅ is proper, then R^min ≅ T_{∅,m∅} and H₁(Y, O)_{m∅} is free over it, together with the addenda of Theorem 1.3 (μ = 1 when H₁ ⊗ Q ≠ 0; T_m a complete intersection when dim T_m = 0). The hypotheses of Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 are those corrected in sourceIssues.

Layers:
1. Weight-one Hecke modules on the modular curves X = X₁(N)/H, X₀(Q), X_Δ(Q). The anaemic and full Hecke algebras T^an, T, T_∅ and their maximal ideals. The Pontryagin-dual coherent homology H_i(X, L) := H^i(X, (Ω¹ ⊗ L*)_{K/O})^∨, with its Hecke action and duality with H^{1−i}. The Hecke-linear isomorphism Ψ in weight one. Lemma 3.7 and Remark 3.4 as corrected. The auxiliary Γ₁(q)-level of Remark 3.10.
2. Taylor–Wiles levels in weight one: Lemmas 3.5 and 3.6 (degeneracy maps ψ, ψ^∨, the U_x-relations and the old space); the Hecke-equivariant Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence; Proposition 3.8 (balancedness of H₀(X_Δ(Q), ω)_m over O[Δ]).
3. Galois representations over torsion weight-one Hecke algebras: Theorem 3.11, the doubling Lemma 3.16, Lemmas 3.17 and 3.24, and the global doubling ideal. Import R̃†, R†, R^unr and Lemma 3.22 (J = I) from LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7, where this extraction sends them by a source route.
4. Minimal R = T in weight one: the patching data, Theorem 3.26, Theorem 1.4 without vexing primes, rank one, Corollaries 1.5 and 1.6.
5. Vexing primes: the level groups U, V (corrected), the Conrad–Diamond–Taylor types σ_x (imported from GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R16.2–R16.3), the bundles L_σ ⊃ L_σ^sub, Lemmas 3.27–3.28, Corollary 3.29, Theorem 3.30 and its four steps.
6. Multiplicity two: harmless primes and the characters φ; R̃_φ ≅ T_{φ,m}, Cohen–Macaulay of type 3; T_m ≅ T_{1,m} ⊗ O[Φ]; the count from type 3 to multiplicity 2; Theorem 4.8 and Remark 4.12.
7. Bianchi forms: Conjecture A (parts (1)–(4)) as an explicit Prop-valued hypothesis, never a conclusion; associated and non-Eisenstein ideals; Lemmas 5.6, 5.8 and 5.9; Proposition 5.10 (balanced H₁); Theorem 5.11; Theorems 1.2 and 1.3. Record §5.5 (why PGL₂ and cyclotomic determinant) as a design note.

Imports: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3, R03.5 (Definitions 2.1–2.2, Proposition 2.3) and R03.6. GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1–R04.6 (Definition 3.1, R_Q, Propositions 3.2–3.3, 5.1–5.2). LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2 and L7. ModularCurvesPartII R13.1–R14.4. AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.1–R15.5 (Katz forms, the Hasse invariant, θ, the weight-one T_p of Gross, Edixhoven's twisted duality, all of which this extraction routes there). SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.1–R20.3 (m∅ via Serre's conjecture and companion forms; the Gross exact sequence). ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.0–ALS.5 and IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.1–IHG.2 for Y(K), Hecke operators, the boundary and Poincaré duality. GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R16.2–R16.4 (types; multiplicity one). tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves, tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev.

Relation to other proposals. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 proposes GL2ModularityLiftingPositiveDefect: integral non-minimal R = T in positive defect, over Shimura curves in weight one and PGL₂ over any number field under Conjectures A–D. That Part II starts where this one stops, and its brief says it imports what this extraction routes. So the weight-one Hecke machinery, the doubling argument and the Bianchi hypotheses are planned here once. The GL_n theory of Part 2 of the paper is a separate Part II of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure.

Acceptance:
- ρ̄ with no vexing primes, where Theorem 3.26 applies directly.
- Mestre's example of torsion in H¹(X₁(N), ω) (Edixhoven 2006, Appendix A), showing that T_m need not be O-flat.
- Serre's X_H(13) example (footnote 3), which shows the stack convention matters.
- The three cases of Theorem 3.11.
- An imaginary quadratic F whose class number is divisible by p. This is the issue of §5.5, and it is why the layer works with PGL₂ and cyclotomic determinant. Review addendum (REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18): the design job must also respect the review's new source issues. E221: define L_σ on X_{U_i(Q)} and X_0(x) at level V, as the paper does for L_σ^sub; flat pullback from X_U is only a subsheaf at doubly ramified cusps. E224: at v | N with v ≡ −1 mod p and ρ̄|G_v a ramified twist of (ω̄ ∗; 0 1), replace R_{v,φ} by its Steinberg quotient. E226: pin the diamond characters in Lemma 5.8. Recorded issues E1–E217 were all confirmed, with the scope corrections noted on each.
routes.reason: Part 1 of the paper is GL₂ modularity lifting, the direction of GL2ModularityLifting, but beyond it: that roadmap follows KW II with defect ℓ₀ = 0, one-degree Hecke modules and Wiles's numerical coincidence. Weight-one forms over Q (coherent H⁰ and H¹) and PGL₂ over imaginary quadratic fields (Betti H₁ and H₂) have ℓ₀ = 1: the Hecke modules are balanced rather than free and are not O-flat, and nothing in the atlas proves R = T for them. The GL₂ positive-defect Part II proposed by PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 is its non-minimal continuation and says it imports what this extraction routes, so the minimal-level theory is planned here once, under a distinct id. Review: accepted. The deduction of Theorem 1.2 from Theorem 1.3, the cartesian degeneracy squares and two steps of Theorem 3.30(4) were added. The L_σ construction must be done at level V (E221), and the §4.1 R = T isomorphisms need the Steinberg quotient at v ≡ −1 mod p mod-p Steinberg primes (E224). The distinct id is kept: make_queue.py appends one design job per accepted route and does not merge two papers' routes with the same id.

routes.title: Reusable infrastructure for potential automorphy over CM fields, Part II: conditional automorphy lifting for GL_n over arbitrary number fields
routes.brief:
Reusable infrastructure for potential automorphy over CM fields (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure) builds the interfaces of Allen et al., "Potential automorphy over CM fields" (ACC+). These cover integral cohomology on complexes, degree shifting, derived Ihara avoidance, Taylor–Wiles primes, ultrapatching and compatible systems, and they are used to prove unconditional automorphy lifting over CM fields. It has no layer for the conditional framework from which that work grew. That framework is automorphy lifting for GL_n over an arbitrary number field F, where the cohomology of the locally symmetric spaces of Res_{F/Q} PGL_n localised at a non-Eisenstein m occupies l0 + 1 degrees [q0, q0 + l0], under a conjecture that supplies Galois representations, local–global compatibility and vanishing outside that range. This Part II starts there. It follows Part 2 of Calegari–Geraghty, "Modularity lifting beyond the Taylor–Wiles method", Invent. Math. 211 (2018) 297–433 (§§5.16, 7.1, 8–9; arXiv:1207.4224v2).

Final theorems, as the paper states them, with the corrections recorded in sourceIssues:
- Theorem 5.16. Assume Conjecture B. Let F be a number field, n ≥ 1, and p > n unramified in F. Let r: G_F → GL_n(O) be continuous and unramified almost everywhere, with the following properties:
  - r is crystalline at v | p, with Hodge–Tate weights {0, …, n−1} of multiplicity one at each embedding;
  - r̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} is absolutely irreducible, F(ad⁰ r̄) does not contain ζ_p, and r̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is big;
  - r is odd at real places;
  - r has unipotent inertia at ramified x ∤ p, with N(x) ≡ 1 mod p where r̄ is unramified;
  - det r = ε^{n(n−1)/2};
  - either r̄ comes from a cuspidal π0 of trivial infinitesimal character, with good reduction at p, which satisfies the same local condition; or r̄ is Serre modular of minimal level and r is ramified only where r̄ is.

  Then r is modular: L(r, s) = L(π, s) for a regular algebraic cusp form π of GL_n(A_F) with trivial infinitesimal character.
- Theorem 9.19. Under the standing hypotheses of §9.5, H^{q0}(Y, K/O)^∨_m is a nearly faithful R_S-module. Theorem 5.16 is deduced from it. The deduction is not written in the paper, and the design job must write it: produce m from (8a) or (8b), check that r has type S, and pass from a point of R_S to a cuspidal π by the boundary vanishing of Conjecture B(4)(b).
- Lemma 9.6: for n = 2, condition (5) of Conjecture B holds at every Taylor–Wiles prime. It is proved with the amalgam PSL₂(O_F[1/x]) = Γ¹ ∗_{Γ¹₀(x)} Γ¹ and Lyndon's exact sequence.

Layers:
1. Arithmetic quotients Y(K), Y₀(Q), Y₁(Q) of Res PGL_n with Iwahori level at R and the local systems O(ψ). The Hecke operators T_{α,k}, T_{𝔞,k} with the normalisation corrected in sourceIssues. The Hecke algebras T^an_{Q,ψ} and T_{Q,ψ} of Definition 9.1, acting on cohomology with O/ϖ^n coefficients. Non-Eisenstein ideals. Import ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.0–ALS.6, IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.2–IHG.3 and AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.4.
2. Conjecture B, as explicit Prop-valued hypotheses, never conclusions: the residual r̄_m and its lift r_m, and parts (1)–(5). Record the dévissage remark, the cases of (4)(a) known by the congruence subgroup property (Remark 9.3), and what later work proved: Scholze's torsion representations modulo a nilpotent ideal; Newton–Thorne; the local–global compatibility of ACC+ and Caraiani–Newton. (4) is still open.
3. Condition (5) at Taylor–Wiles primes: Lemma 9.6 for n = 2 (degeneracy maps; the amalgam, imported from ModularCurvesPartII R14.4 and ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2; U_x²). §9.4 as the conditional route in general: it uses the local theorem, Theorem 9.16, which this extraction routes to SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.5.
4. Complexes: the minimal perfect complexes D̃_N and D̃^χ_N over O[Δ_N] computing localised homology, built from §7.1 (planned in ALS.1, ALS.3, IHG.2 and DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P7), and the localising operator of §7.1.
5. Galois side: import GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.x, G7 and G8 (S_Q, S_Q^χ, T-framed rings, Lemma 8.3, Proposition 8.4, the numerical coincidence Proposition 8.5 with the corrected count), LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 and R08.2 (Fontaine–Laffaille rings, Taylor's R¹_v and R^χ_v, Lemma 8.2), ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.5–R02.6, and the invariants l0 and q0 from AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1 and AF.4.
6. Patching and the main theorem: the patching data for Proposition 6.6 (Theorem 6.3, Theorem 6.4 and Proposition 6.6 are planned in DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P8, P9 and R03.6, with the hypotheses corrected in sourceIssues), P²_∞ nearly faithful, transfer to the unipotent data by Taylor's Ihara avoidance, Theorem 9.19 and Theorem 5.16. Export Theorem 5.16, conditional on Conjecture B, to ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2, where this extraction routes Theorem 1.1.

Relation to other proposals. GL2ModularityLiftingDefectOne (this extraction) holds the l0 = 1 cases for GL₂. GL2ModularityLiftingPositiveDefect (PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24) holds the non-minimal PGL₂ theory; its Conjectures A–D are the n = 2 specialisations of these hypotheses, and it should import them from here. The ACC+ route of the parent roadmap proves unconditional versions over CM fields, and this Part II must not duplicate PA.3–PA.4. It states the conditional hypotheses and reuses those interfaces.

Acceptance:
- n = 1 (§8.2). l0 = r1 + r2 − 1, and the method returns R^unr ≅ Z_p[Cl(O_F) ⊗ Z_p]; the argument is circular.
- n = 2 over an imaginary quadratic field, which should specialise to GL2ModularityLiftingDefectOne's Bianchi case.
- A totally real F with l0 = 0 for n = 2, which recovers KW II-style lifting. Review addendum (REV-PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18): Lemma 9.6 must be proved at m̃ = (m, U_x − α_x), not at the anaemic m (E229); Theorem 9.19 states near faithfulness only; §10 needs N₂ > 2n + 1 (E213) and the simultaneous HSBT reduction (E214).
routes.reason: Part 2 of the paper proves automorphy lifting for GL_n over any number field in any defect l0, conditional on Conjecture B. PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure plans the unconditional descendant of this method over CM fields (derived patching, Taylor–Wiles primes, Ihara avoidance). The conditional GL_n theory over arbitrary fields — the Hecke algebras on cohomology mod ϖ^n, Conjecture B as hypotheses, Lemma 9.6, the complexes D̃_N and Theorem 9.19 — goes in its direction but beyond its CM-field scope, and no layer plans it. It reuses the parent's interfaces and the planned patching algebra (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P8, P9, R03.6) rather than re-planning them. Review: accepted. 'Serre modular of minimal level' was added. Lemma 9.6's proof needs localization at m̃ = (m, U_x − α_x) (E229).

routes.title: Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes
routes.brief:
Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms (AutomorphicBundles) constructs automorphic vector bundles, their canonical and subcanonical extensions to toroidal compactifications, classical forms as their sections, and Hecke actions and Fourier expansions (B3–B5). These are statements about sections in characteristic zero. The roadmap has no layer for the integral coherent cohomology of these bundles over O/ϖ^n, or for Hecke operators on all cohomological degrees. Nor does it have one for perfect complexes over O/ϖ^n[Δ] that compute this cohomology with lifted Hecke actions, which patching in the coherent case needs. This Part II starts there. It follows §7.2 of Calegari–Geraghty, "Modularity lifting beyond the Taylor–Wiles method", Invent. Math. 211 (2018) 297–433 (pp. 395–401; arXiv:1207.4224v2), which constructs these complexes for smooth proper integral models of Shimura varieties and their arithmetic toroidal compactifications.

Final result, as the paper states it (§7.2, p. 400). Let Y = X_Δ(Q) → X = X₀(Q) be a finite étale Galois cover with group Δ, a finite abelian p-group, of smooth proper O-schemes. These are integral models of Shimura varieties, or Lan's arithmetic toroidal compactifications. Let 𝓔 be an automorphic vector bundle (its canonical or subcanonical extension in the toroidal case), R = A[Δ] with A = O/ϖ^n, and m a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra generated by good Hecke operators and operators at the Taylor–Wiles primes Q. Then there is a perfect complex of R-modules, lim_m T^m C_n for a suitable Hecke operator T, whose homology is the coherent homology H_i(Y, 𝓔_A)_m := H^i(Y, 𝓔* ⊗ ω_Y ⊗ A)^∨_m, and on which each Hecke operator T_γ acts through a lift to the complex.

Layers:
1. Setting and coherent homology: the covers, the bundles 𝓔 pulled back along f, coherent homology as the Pontryagin dual of H^i(Y, 𝓔* ⊗ ω_Y ⊗ O/ϖ^n), and its comparison with H^{d−i} by Grothendieck–Serre duality with trace (imported from AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension, where this extraction routes the general duality statement).
2. Perfect complexes over A[Δ]: Nakajima's Čech complex for an affine cover and the projectivity over k[Δ] of N ⊗_A B for a Galois étale Spec B → Spec A (Nakajima, Lemma 1). Lemma 7.7 gives freeness modulo ϖ^n, using DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P7's Lemmas 7.5–7.6 and Mumford's lemma replacing the Čech complex by a perfect one.
3. Hecke operators: for γ ∈ G(A^{∞,p}), the correspondence Y^γ → Y from a suitable toroidal compactification of level L ∩ γLγ^{-1} (imported from ShimuraCompactifications C3–C5), and the isomorphism φ: π₂*𝓔 ≅ π₁*𝓔 (Lan, Theorem 2.15(4)(c); every automorphic bundle comes from the Hodge bundle). T_γ is defined by the Faltings–Chai trace-free pairing tr(π₁*(x) ∪ φπ₂*(y)), with trace H^d(Y^γ, ω) → A.
4. Lifting to complexes: T̃_γ as an element of Hom in D^b(A[Δ]) by composing pullback, composition and the duality morphism, and its lift to C_n^∨ by Stacks 08FQ. The trace morphism RΓ(Y^γ, ω[d]) → A[0] is not an isomorphism, and the construction must be corrected as recorded in sourceIssues. Then comes localisation at m by the Hecke idempotent, imported from IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.2 and PadicFamilies L0a.

Imports: AutomorphicBundles B3–B5; ShimuraCompactifications C3 and C5; PELModuli; AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension; SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2; DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P7 (perfect complexes, derived coefficient change); IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.2; tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction for Čech cohomology and flat base change on curves.

Consumers. GL2ModularityLiftingPositiveDefect (proposed by PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24) needs these complexes for the weight-one cohomology of Shimura curves (its Proposition 14.1) and should import them. The coherent case of Calegari–Geraghty's general patching (Theorem 6.3) consumes the localised complexes. GL2ModularityLiftingDefectOne (this extraction) works with modules in weight one and needs only degrees 0 and 1 on modular curves, but it should use these definitions of coherent homology and Hecke operators.

Acceptance:
- The modular curve X₁(N) with 𝓔 = ω: the complexes compute H_0 and H_1 of §3.2.4, with the Hecke action of §3.2.3.
- Shimura curves X^𝔇 with ω, as in the consumer above.
- A non-compact case: a Hilbert modular surface or a Siegel threefold with a subcanonical extension, where the Hecke correspondence needs a change of cone decomposition.
routes.reason: §7.2 builds perfect complexes over O/ϖ^n[Δ] computing the coherent cohomology of automorphic bundles on integral models of Shimura varieties, with Hecke operators lifted to the complexes. AutomorphicBundles owns automorphic bundles, their extensions and Hecke actions on sections in characteristic zero (B3–B5), but plans nothing integral or in higher degree. This is its direction beyond its present scope, and both this paper's coherent case and PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24's weight-one Shimura-curve complexes need it. Review: accepted.

The paper's patching algebra is already planned here: §2 (balanced modules, Proposition 2.3) in R03.5, whose reviewed node transcribes it from this paper, and §6 (Lemma 6.2, Theorems 6.3–6.4, Proposition 6.6) in P8, P9 and R03.6. What is missing is local algebra of the same kind. R03.3, the owner of depth, Cohen–Macaulay and Gorenstein theory, gets canonical modules and their behaviour along regular sequences, Lemma 4.1 (Hom_{Z_p}(A, Z_p) is the canonical module of a finite flat Cohen–Macaulay A), Lemma 4.2 (with the O-flatness hypothesis it needs), Hilbert series and Lemma 4.4 (corrected), graded regular sequences, O[Δ] as a complete intersection, and BLGHT's completed tensor product lemma. R03.5 gets the defect over O[Δ] computed from coinvariants, used in Propositions 3.8 and 5.10. P7 gets Lemmas 7.5–7.6 and 'projective over a local ring is free', the coefficient facts behind the coherent complexes. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 routed dualizing complexes and Gorenstein duality to R03.3 in the same way. The printed forms of Theorem 6.3's hypotheses (c)–(d), of Lemma 6.2 and of Theorem 6.4(3), which the reviewed P8, P9 and R03.6 nodes reproduce, need the corrections recorded in sourceIssues. Review: accepted. The duplicate item canonical-module-regular-sequence-facts was removed; Lemma 4.2 is corrected to 'B or C O-flat' (E72).

The local rings of the weight-one and multiplicity-two arguments belong to the owner of local deformation rings. L7 (ordinary and potentially semistable rings, their components and dimension) and L8 (determinant-ordinary conditions against flags) get R̃† for trivial ρ̄|G_p: Kisin's quotient with an eigenvalue of Frobenius, Snowden's equations, the unramified quotients, the unramified ideal I and doubling ideal J with Lemma 3.22 (J = I), and Theorem 4.3 (R̃† is normal Cohen–Macaulay of relative dimension 4, of type 3, with the Hilbert-series computations of Lemmas 4.5–4.7). R08.2 gets Lemma 4.11 (the rings R_{v,φ}, v ≠ p, are complete intersections with smooth generic fibre, including the hypersurface case O⟦x1,…,x4⟧/(r) of footnote 5), and R08.1 Kisin's description of completed local rings of generic fibres. Snowden (Math. Z. 2018) and Geraghty (Math. Ann. 2019) are co-sources. Review: accepted. The classification of the non-smooth cases of Lemma 4.11 (with the case E89 adds) and the Taylor–Wiles local tangent dimension (tw-local-selmer-dimension, whose cited layers disown it) were added.

The Hecke operators of §3.2.3 on H^i(X, ω^{⊗n}_A) and on the cusps, the operators U_x and W_x (with W_x² = x^n⟨x⟩), and the Hecke-equivariance of the cuspidal sequence go to R15.2, the owner of integral Hecke theory on geometric forms; that layer should plan them for i = 0, 1 and for torsion coefficients. Edixhoven's operator w_ζ and the Hecke-twisted duality Φ (Φ∘T_x = x^{1−n}T_x^∨∘Φ, [Edixhoven 1992, Prop. 7.3]) and Gross's Hecke operator T_p on weight-one Katz forms mod ϖ^m go to R15.3, beside the Hasse invariant and Frobenius/Verschiebung. Review: accepted. The Fricke map w_x (planned nowhere) joins W_x here, with Edixhoven's Kodaira–Spencer isogeny lemma.

Weight-one modularity of ρ̄ at its Serre level (the maximal ideal m∅, from Serre's conjecture with the companion forms of Gross and Coleman–Voloch) goes to R20.3, consistently with PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 and PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25. So do the inputs to Theorem 4.8 that are statements about J₁(N*): the multiplicity of m (R20.1), the known multiplicity-one cases (Mazur, Mazur–Ribet, Buzzard; R20.2–R20.3), Wiese's multiplicity ≥ 2 in the scalar case, and Gross's ordinary exact sequence of Tate modules (R20.3). The new multiplicity-two argument itself is in GL2ModularityLiftingDefectOne. Review: accepted.

R04.2 (representability and universal rings) gets Lemma 4.14 (R[1/p] is reduced when the generic fibre has finitely many points with finite image; corrected) with Mazur's 'traces generate the universal ring', and the rank-one examples of §8.2: the representation from class field theory and R^unr ≅ Z_p[Cl(O_F) ⊗ Z_p]. R04.5 (Taylor–Wiles primes) gets the rank-one existence of Taylor–Wiles primes, which works exactly when ζ_p ∉ F. The paper is also a source for R04.5 in weight one over Q (Propositions 3.2–3.3), for imaginary quadratic fields (Propositions 5.1–5.2), and for the l0 count in rank n (Propositions 8.4–8.5), which are planned. Review: accepted.

The Selmer-group numerics go to the owner of Poitou–Tate and the Greenberg–Wiles formula: the rank-one example dim H¹_L(F, F_p) − dim H¹_{L*}(F, μ_p) = −(r1 + r2 − 1) (R02.5), the archimedean term Σ_{v|∞} dim H⁰(F_v, ad⁰V) = [F:Q]n(n−1)/2 + l0 behind the numerical coincidence (R02.6), and the absence of Z_p-extensions unramified at all primes above p used in Lemma 4.14 (R02.3). Review: accepted.

Two notation-level definitions: the unramified character λ(α) of a decomposition group (R01.2) and oddness of an n-dimensional representation at a real place, trace of complex conjugation in {−1, 0, 1} (G7, the dimension-general API, beside the polarized sign condition). Review: accepted.

The level subgroups of §5.2 (Γ₀(v^c), Γ₁(v^c), Γ_p(v^c) and K_Q ⊂ L_Q for PGL₂ over an imaginary quadratic field) and of §9.1 (the (1, n−1)-parahoric and its normal subgroup at Taylor–Wiles primes, Iwahori level at R) go to ALS.0 and ALS.3 with the arithmetic quotients and change-of-level maps, as PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 routed its PGL₂ levels. The degeneracy maps of Lemma 9.6 and their composite go to ALS.3. The definition of Eisenstein ideals (Definition 5.5), with the boundary vanishing of Lemma 5.9(3), goes to ALS.4. Review: accepted.

The invariants l0 = rank G(R) − rank K∞ − rank A and q0 (with 2q0 + l0 = dim of the symmetric space), their explicit values for Res_{F/Q} PGL_n (§8.4) and PGL₂ (Remark 5.14), and the Borel–Wallach theorem that tempered cohomological representations contribute exactly in degrees [q0, q0 + l0], belong to the owner of real reductive groups and relative Lie algebra cohomology. Review: accepted.

Two Hecke-algebra facts: the localising operator T = ∏P_x ∏P_i, an element of every other maximal ideal but not of m, whose limit e_T cuts out the localisation (IHG.2), and 'a module killed by the Cayley–Hamilton ideal of an absolutely irreducible ρ̄ is ρ̄^μ' (Boston–Lenstra–Ribet), used for J₁(N*)[m] in Theorem 4.8 (IHG.1). Review: accepted.

The Conrad–Diamond–Taylor types σ_x at vexing primes and their local multiplicity one ([CDT99, §§4.2, 5; Lemma 4.2.4(3)]) are statements about smooth representations of GL₂(Q_x) and local Langlands, owned by R16.2–R16.3. The vexing-prime layer of GL2ModularityLiftingDefectOne imports them. Review: accepted.

§9.4.1 is local representation theory of GL_n(F_x) over O/ϖ^k, with ℓ ≠ p, in the block of an unramified principal series with distinct Satake parameters. It covers Vignéras's semisimple mod-ℓ correspondence and 'associated to ρ̄', supercuspidal support and Emerton–Helm's Ext¹ criterion, Lemmas 9.9–9.12, Corollary 9.13 (the block as modules over ⊗(A[T]/(T^q − 1) ⊗ A⟦X⟧), with separate variables for each i), Lemma 9.14, Remark 9.15, the ordinary projector e_α and Theorem 9.16 (H^k(G(O_x), M) ≅ e_α H^k(U₀(x), M)), with CHT Lemma 3.2.2 as the degree-zero case. SR.5 owns ℓ ≠ p integral families and blocks for GL_n after Helm. SR.0 owns the smooth category, where 'locally admissible' belongs. The consumer is the Conjecture-B Part II of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure proposed here. Review: accepted. The parahoric-invariants computation behind Theorem 9.16 and the vanishing of Ext between distinct torus characters were added.

Theorem 1.1 is an endpoint: assuming Conjecture B, every elliptic curve over every number field is potentially modular (ML.2) and satisfies Sato–Tate (ML.3). ML.0 registers endpoints with an explicit known, conditional or conjectural status, and ML.1's acceptance forbids claiming the unconditional statement. So Theorem 1.1 is recorded as conditional on Conjecture B, imported from the proposed PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure Part II, with its proof in §10: odd symmetric powers via the Dwork family, BLGHT Theorem 6.4 and Moret–Bailly (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1), then HSBT's reduction. The remark after Lemma 4.14 (when Buzzard–Taylor's hypotheses hold) goes to ML.1. Review: accepted. The twisted modular curve X_E(q) was added; the §10 items now use N₂ > 2n + 1, the E216 relabelling and BLGHT II's Proposition 6.2 as printed.
The flat Kummer sequence 0 → O_F^×/O_F^{×p} → H¹_fppf(O_F, μ_p) → Cl(F)[p] → 0, which computes the dual Selmer group of §8.2, belongs to the owner of fppf cohomology on schemes. Review: accepted.

Grothendieck–Serre ('Verdier') duality with trace for smooth proper schemes of relative dimension d over O/ϖ^n, as §7.2 uses it, extends coherent cohomology and base change beyond curves, which A0-extension owns. The proposed AutomorphicBundles Part II imports it. Review: accepted. Dévissage and cofiniteness for K/O coefficients on curves over O were added.

Remark 9.3 verifies Conjecture B(4)(a) for GL₂ over CM fields of degree 2 or 4 and for GL₃/Q by the congruence subgroup property. Bass–Milnor–Serre's theorem for SL_n(O_{F,S}), n ≥ 3, comes from the same paper and the same Mennicke-symbol arguments that U.4 plans for SK₁(O_{F,S}) = 0. Serre's SL₂ case is part of the same source. Review: accepted.

The Lyndon (Mayer–Vietoris) exact sequence for the cohomology of an amalgamated product, used in Lemma 9.6, is the tool of R14.4's Ihara-lemma proofs 'using the relevant group/tree geometry'. Review: accepted.

Ihara's theorem, from Serre's Trees, that PSL₂(F_x) is an amalgam of two copies of PSL₂(O_x) over the Iwahori subgroup and PGL₂(F_x) is not (Remark 9.7), comes from the SL₂ tree that RG2.2 plans. Review: accepted.

The GL₁ example of §8.2 (X_Q = F^×\A_F^×/U_Q A∞⁰ is a union of tori (S¹)^{r1+r2−1} over the ray class group, H⁰ = Z_p[RCl(Q)/p^n], and l0 = r1 + r2 − 1) is AA.5's GL₁ validation of the adelic quotient. Review: accepted.

Finiteness of the local-condition deformation ring R_φ over O in Theorem 4.8 comes from Thorne's generalisation (Theorem 10.2 of Thorne 2012) of KW II's finiteness theorem, which R24.1 plans. Review: accepted.

sourceIssues.locator: Abstract (p. 298) and §1 Introduction (p. 305), compared with the §4.1 set-up for Theorem 4.8 (p. 361) and Lemma 4.11 (pp. 364–365). arXiv v2 has the same text ("completely solved", l. 316; same parenthetical on twisting before Thm 4.8). arXiv v1 is also the same: intro, and §3.8 Theorem 3.25 with the same twist-minimal hypothesis.
sourceIssues.printed: p. 305 (§1): "In the process of proving our main result, we also completely solve the problem (for p odd) of determining the multiplicity of an irreducible modular representation ρ̄ in the Jacobian J_1(N*)[m], where N* is the minimal level such that ρ̄ arises in weight two. In particular, we prove that when ρ̄ is unramified at p and ρ̄(Frob_p) is a scalar, then the multiplicity of ρ̄ is two (see Theorem 4.8). (In all other cases, the multiplicity was already known to be one—and in the exceptional cases we consider, the multiplicity was also known to be ≥2)." Abstract, p. 298: "Moreover, we also completely solve the problem (for p odd) of determining the multiplicity of an irreducible modular representation ρ̄ in the Jacobian J_1(N), where N is the minimal level such that ρ̄ arises in weight two." p. 361 (§4.1, set-up before Thm 4.8): "Assume that ρ̄ has minimal conductor amongst all its twists at all other primes (one can always twist ρ̄ to satisfy these condition)."
sourceIssues.correction: In the abstract and introduction, limit the multiplicity claim to ρ̄ that have minimal conductor amongst their twists at primes ≠ p. That is the hypothesis of Theorem 4.8. Twist-minimality at p is automatic in the scalar case, where ρ̄|G_p is unramified. The alternative is to give a separate argument for non-twist-minimal ρ̄. Theorem 4.8 as stated in §4.1 needs no change.
sourceIssues.reason:
I rendered pp. 298, 305 and 361–366 and checked them against the text above.

1. The claims do not match. The abstract and introduction claim multiplicity two for every irreducible modular ρ̄ (p odd) at its own minimal weight-2 level. The classical multiplicity-one results cited in Remark 4.9 (Mazur, Gross, Edixhoven, ...) are stated without twist-minimality. Theorem 4.8, however, is proved only under the hypothesis that ρ̄ has minimal conductor among its twists. The only link between the two is the parenthetical "(one can always twist ρ̄ to satisfy these condition)". That remark is true, but it does not show that multiplicity is unchanged by twisting: ρ̄ and ρ̄⊗ψ̄ sit at different levels N(ρ̄)p and N(ρ̄⊗ψ̄)p, with different Jacobians and Hecke algebras.

2. The multiplicity depends on the Hecke algebra. The proof of Theorem 4.8 uses T_pG^0 ≅ T_m and T_pG^e = Hom(T_m, Z_p), so dim J[m] = 1 + (number of generators of ω_{T_m}). Multiplicity two therefore means T_m has type 3. This is a property of T_m, and T_m changes under twisting.

3. A concrete example where T_m changes. Let ρ̄ = ρ̄_0⊗χ̄, with ρ̄_0 twist-minimal and unramified at a prime v ∤ N_0 p, and χ̄ tame of conductor v. Then ρ̄^{I_v} = 0, so every lift has conductor exactly v² and every lift appears at level N(ρ̄)p, with U_v = 0. If ρ̄_0(Frob_v) has eigenvalue ratio ≡ v, then Ribet's level-raised forms (Steinberg at v, level N_0vp) twisted by χ̃ are extra newforms of conductor v² in T_m(ρ̄). They have no counterpart in T_{m_0}(ρ̄_0) at level N_0p. So T_m(ρ̄) corresponds to the unrestricted deformation problem at v, while T_{m_0}(ρ̄_0) corresponds to the unramified one.

4. The proof does not carry over word for word. The proof of Lemma 4.11 lists the non-smooth cases only under twist-minimality. In the example above, R_v ≅ R_v^unrestricted(ρ̄_0|G_v). Its unramified and Steinberg components meet at characteristic-0 points (unramified lifts with eigenvalue ratio v), where H^2(G_v, ad^0ρ) ≠ 0. So "R_v[1/p] formally smooth" fails, and that property is what the text uses when applying Kisin's method to get R̃[1/p] = T[1/p]. The paper's own remark on p. 363 also uses twist-minimality to exclude v ≡ 1 mod p with ρ̄^{I_v} = 0.

5. The result is probably still true. R_v is still a complete intersection, and weight-2 points avoid the intersection locus by Ramanujan. So multiplicity two is plausible at non-minimal level too, but the paper gives no argument for it.

Conclusion: this is a gap in the reduction to the twist-minimal case, and it affects the claim in the abstract and introduction. Theorem 4.8 itself, as stated, is correct. Defence tried and failed. (1) The quantity is not twist-invariant by any formal argument. Twisting ρ̄ = ρ̄_0⊗χ̄ (χ̄ of conductor x ≠ p) changes N(ρ̄), N*, the curve J_1(N*) and the Hecke algebra T. (2) If ρ̄ is not twist-minimal at x, then ρ̄^{I_x} = 0. Every lift then has conductor cond(ρ̄|G_x), so every lift of ρ̄|G_x shows up at level Γ_1(N). After twisting back, m at level N(ρ̄)p also sees non-minimal forms for ρ̄_0. Examples are χ-twists of forms that are Steinberg at x (conductor x²) when the level-raising condition holds, or of ramified principal series of p-power type when x ≡ 1 mod p. So T_m is not the twist of T_{m_0} at level N(ρ̄_0)p. When no such extra forms exist, a Chebotarev/trace argument does identify the two Hecke algebras, but not in general. (3) The paper's proof really does use minimality. On p. 362, Φ is 'the only twists' preserving minimal-conductor lifts only under minimality; when x ≡ 1 mod p and ρ̄ is non-minimal at x, the characters of Z_p⊗(Z/x)^× also qualify. On p. 363 the paper itself says the twist-uniqueness 'is not true when v ≡ 1 mod p and ρ̄ has trivial invariants under I_v' and removes this case by the minimality assumption. Lemma 4.11 lists only the non-smooth cases that can occur for twist-minimal ρ̄. For a non-minimal ρ̄|G_x = χ̄⊗(unramified, Frobenius-eigenvalue ratio ≡ x mod p), R_{x,φ} is isomorphic to the unrestricted fixed-determinant ring of an unramified representation. Its unramified and Steinberg components meet in the generic fibre at the points μ⊕με, where H²(G_x, ad⁰ρ) ≠ 0. So the claim that the generic fibre is formally smooth fails, and with it the stated input to Kisin's R[1/p] = T[1/p]. (4) No nearby statement closes the gap. Remark 4.12 concerns J_H, and the parenthetical '(one can always twist ρ̄…)' only says that a twist-minimal twist exists. The general statement is very plausibly true: the extra local rings are complete intersections of type 1, and modular points avoid the singular locus. But the paper gives no proof of it, so the introduction and abstract claim more than Theorem 4.8 proves. Consequences: §4.1 opens with 'Although this is not needed for our main results', and nothing later cites Theorem 4.8. Only the claim in the abstract and introduction is affected, and the proposed restriction is right and minimal.

(This is certainly true of the tempered representations which occur in Betti cohomology. According to [9], the range of cohomological degrees to which they occur has length l0 + 1. In the coherent case, the value of l0 will depend on the infinity components πv allowed. That tempered representations occur in a range of length l0, then follows from [10, Theorems 3.4 and 3.5] together with knowledge of L-packets at infinite primes)." (p. 300 = PDF page 4; the same wording is in arXiv v2, lines 131-145.)
sourceIssues.correction: "maximal Q-split torus A" should read "maximal Q-split torus A in the centre of G" (the usual A_G). Then l0 = rank(G) − rank(K) − rank(A), with rank meaning absolute rank of the real group, as in §8.4; this is the qualifier the paper itself uses in §8.2, p. 403: "the maximal Q-split torus in the centre".
sourceIssues.reason:
I checked the rendered page (p. 300 = PDF p. 4) against the transcription above. Read literally, A is a maximal Q-split torus of G. "rank" must mean absolute rank here: §8.4 computes l0 from rank(SL_n(R)) − rank(SO_n(R)), and with real rank you would get Hilbert modular surfaces wrong. Under that reading my own computations give:
(a) GL2/Q: rank G = 2, rank O(2) = 1, Q-rank = 2, so l0 = −1, which is impossible.
(b) Res_{F/Q}GL2 with F imaginary quadratic: complexified Lie algebra gl2 ⊕ gl2 has rank 4, rank U(2) = 2, Q-rank = 2, so l0 = 0 instead of 1.
(c) Res_{F/Q}PGL2 with F imaginary quadratic, the paper's own Part 1 case: 2 − 1 − 1 = 0, but the paper treats this case as l0 = 1 (Part 1 "l0 equals 1"; §8.3 "n = 2 and l0 = 1").
(d) Remark 5.14 (p. 3xx, "l0 = rank(G) − rank(K) for PGL(2)/H ... equal to the number of complex places of H") has no A term. The literal intro formula would give r2 − 1 there.
With A taken as the Q-split torus in the centre, every value comes out right: GL2/Q gives 0, GL2 over imaginary quadratic F gives 1, PGL2 gives 1 (trivial central torus), and Res GL1 gives r1 + r2 − 1, matching §8.2. So the printed definition is wrong as stated and the fix is the missing "in the centre". It is not one of the 47 bracket errors. It is also in the accepted arXiv v2, so it is not a production artifact. On length, the paragraph does say "length l0 + 1" and then "length l0", but each use is correct under its own meaning: number of degrees versus length of the interval. That part is a stylistic inconsistency, not an error. The paper's main convention elsewhere is "range of length l0", including p. 300 below, and Part 2's "degrees of arbitrary length l0" and "range of degrees of length l0".

sourceIssues.correction: Add to Theorem 1.3 a hypothesis, and make §5.1(3) exhaustive to match: for each prime x ∤ p at which ρ̄ is ramified, if ρ̄|I_x is reducible then it is either unipotent or semisimple. Equivalently, ρ̄|I_x is never ≅ ψ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 1) with ∗ ≠ 0 and ψ a non-trivial character. Such a ψ is necessarily quadratic, and this case is the twisted Steinberg type. The analogous twist-minimality assumption "if x ∈ S(ρ̄) and ρ̄|G_x is reducible, then ρ̄^{I_x} ≠ (0)" is imposed in §3.1 (p. 310) for the case over Q. The alternative is to add a fifth local type T: the lift condition ρ|I_x ≅ ⟨ψ⟩ ⊗ unipotent, a matching level K_{Q,x} in §5.2.1(5), and a matching clause in Conjecture A(2). The tangent-space term L_{Q,x} = H^1(G_x/I_x, (ad^0)^{I_x}) and Proposition 5.1 carry over unchanged, because ad^0 does not change under a twist. Both reported corrections are right. Adding the hypothesis is the minimal fix.
sourceIssues.reason:
I checked the rendered pages 302, 369–371, 374 and 379–380.

1. The case is possible and falls outside the paper's types. Take x ∤ p. Since det ρ̄ = ε, the restriction det ρ̄|I_x is trivial. Suppose ρ̄|I_x is reducible but not semisimple. Then the unique I_x-stable line is D_x-stable, so ρ̄|D_x is reducible, with characters χ1, χ2 and a non-zero class in H^1(I_x, χ1χ2^{-1}). Because ℓ ≠ p, this group is H^1(I_x/P, k(χ1χ2^{-1})^P), and it vanishes unless χ1|I_x = χ2|I_x = ψ. Together with ψ^2 = 1 this gives ρ̄|I_x ≅ ψ ⊗ (1 *; 0 1) with * ≠ 0. If ψ ≠ 1, the image contains −1 times a matrix of the form (1 *; 0 1), so ρ̄|I_x is not unipotent in the paper's sense (image inside the matrices (1 *; 0 1)). It is not semisimple, so it is not (c). It is not irreducible, so it is not (a). Since D_x is reducible, it is not (d)/M in the intended sense. So it is none of the types S, P, M, H. The deformation conditions (5)–(8) impose nothing at x, §5.2.1(5) defines K_{Q,v} only for types S, P, M, H, and Conjecture A(2) has no clause for this type. The proof of Theorem 5.11 therefore never reaches this case: it needs R^min, Y = Y(K_∅), the tangent bound of Prop. 5.1 with L_{Q,x} = H^1(G_x/I_x, (ad^0)^{I_x}), and Conjecture A.

2. Theorem 1.3's hypotheses do not exclude the case. Hypothesis (4) is satisfied because D_x is reducible.

3. An explicit example. Take E = 11a1, which has split multiplicative reduction at 11 with v_11(Δ) = 5 and surjective mod-7 image. Let χ be the quadratic character of Q(√−11), which is ramified only at 11. Take p = 7 and F = Q(i), so 7 and 11 are inert in F, and set ρ̄ = ρ̄_{E^χ,7}|G_F.
- The determinant is cyclotomic, and ρ̄ is finite flat at 7 (E^χ has good reduction there).
- At x = (11), ρ̄|I_x = χ|I_11 ⊗ (non-trivial unipotent), since 7 ∤ 5.
- The image of G_{F(ζ_7)} is a normal subgroup of SL_2(F_7) with abelian quotient, so it is all of SL_2(F_7) (SL_2(F_7) is perfect). Hence (3) holds.
- N(x) = 121 ≡ 2 mod 7, so (4) holds.
- The Artin conductor at x is x^2 (ρ̄^{I_x} = 0), and the base change of the level-121 newform E^χ gives modularity at Γ_0(N(ρ̄)).
So Theorem 1.3 as printed applies to this ρ̄, but §5 does not cover it.

4. Side remarks. Read literally, the conditional in §5.1(3)(d) is vacuously true when D_x is reducible. That reading makes things no better, because the levels and the type assignment ("we say that ρ̄|D_x is of type S, P, M or H") would then be undefined at x. Twisting ρ̄ by a global quadratic character would reduce this case to type S, as v1 did, but the published paper does not carry out that reduction and it does not transfer the Y_0(N) statement. The conclusion may even fail as stated at Γ_0(N) level: when N(x) ≡ 1 mod p, Γ_0(x^2) also sees principal series π(ψη, (ψη)^{-1}) with η of p-power order, and these are not minimal lifts. I did not verify this possible failure, so I classify the problem as a gap rather than an error.

On locators: C-K1-0's p. 379 for the "follows from" sentence should be p. 380. X-K6-15's aside that Y_0(N) in Theorem 1.3 should be read as Y(K_∅) (K_∅ uses Γ_p(v^c) for types P, M, H) is plausible, but I did not assess it separately. The case exists and is excluded nowhere. Take x ∤ p. Because det ρ̄ is cyclotomic, det ρ̄|I_x = 1. If ρ̄|I_x is reducible and not split, the extension class lies in H^1(I_x, ψ1ψ2^{-1}). The wild inertia group is pro-ℓ with ℓ ≠ p, so this group vanishes unless ψ1 = ψ2 = ψ. Then ψ^2 = 1. With ψ = 1 we get type S. With ψ ≠ 1 we get ρ̄|I_x ≅ ψ ⊗ (non-split unipotent). The line fixed by I_x is D_x-stable, so ρ̄|D_x is reducible and hypothesis (4) of Theorem 1.3 says nothing at x.

This ρ̄ matches none of the lift conditions (5) S, (6) P, (7) M or (8) H on p. 369:
- It is not unipotent.
- It is not a direct sum ψ ⊕ ψ^{-1}.
- ρ̄|D_x is reducible, which rules out M.
- It is not irreducible.
Condition (4) covers only x ∉ S(ρ̄). So R^min puts no condition at x, and that does not match the Selmer condition L_{Q,x} = unramified classes used in Proposition 5.1. The level K_{Q,v} in §5.2.1(5) is defined only for types S/P/M/H. Conjecture A(2) speaks only to S and P, so it gives no local-global compatibility at x for R^min → T_m.

Defence tried and failed:
- Read literally, §5.1(3)(d) is an implication. It is then vacuous whenever ρ̄|D_x is reducible, and §5.1(3) becomes logically equivalent to Theorem 1.3(4). On that reading §5 itself admits the case and leaves it untreated.
- On the intended reading, (a)–(d) list the types, so §5.1(3) excludes the case, but Theorem 1.3 does not.
- Either way, "Theorem 1.3 follows from Theorem 5.11" fails for these ρ̄.
- No nearby statement fills the gap. The §3.1 twist-minimality assumption applies only over Q. The global twist in arXiv v1 was dropped.

Such ρ̄ really occur. Take E = 11a1, which has split multiplicative reduction at 11 with v_11(Δ) = 5, and p = 3 ∤ 5. Twist E by χ_{-11}, which is unramified at 3. Then E^χ has good reduction at 3. Restrict to F = Q(i), where 3 and 11 are inert. At x = (11), ρ̄ = E^χ[3] has cyclotomic determinant and ρ̄|I_x ≅ χ|I_x ⊗ (non-split unipotent) with χ|I_x ≠ 1. It is finite flat at 3, and its image over F(ζ_3) contains SL_2(F_3), so it is absolutely irreducible. N(x) = 121 ≢ −1 mod 3, and ρ̄ is modular via base change of the level-lowered form. So every hypothesis of Theorem 1.3 holds.

Consequences:
- Nothing later in the paper uses Theorem 1.3 except the deduction of Theorem 1.2.
- Theorem 1.2 is unaffected. There ρ is semi-stable, so ρ̄|I_x is unipotent (type S) or trivial.

sourceIssues.printed: p. 303 (PDF p. 7): "Theorem 1.4 Suppose that p ≥ 3. Let ρ̄ : G_Q → GL_2(k) be an odd continuous irreducible Galois representation of Serre level N. Assume that ρ̄ is unramified at p. Let R^min denote the universal minimal unramified-at-p deformation ring of ρ̄. Then there exists a quotient X_U of X_1(N) and a vector bundle L_σ on X_U such that if T denotes the Hecke algebra of H^1(X_U, ω⊗L_σ), there is an isomorphism R^min ⥲ T_m where m is the maximal ideal of T corresponding to ρ̄. Moreover, H^1(X_U, ω⊗L_σ)_m is free as a T_m-module." p. 310 (PDF p. 14), §3.1: "We further assume that if x ∈ S(ρ̄) and ρ̄|G_x is reducible, then ρ̄^{I_x} ≠ (0). Note that this last condition is always satisfied by a twist of ρ̄ by a character unramified outside of S(ρ̄)." p. 311, Definition 3.1(4): "If x ∈ S(ρ̄) − T(ρ̄) and ρ̄|G_x is reducible, then ρ^{I_x} is a rank one direct summand of ρ as an R-module." (The candidate's quote leaves out the opening "Suppose that p ≥ 3." but is otherwise accurate.)
sourceIssues.correction:
Simplest fix: add the §3.1 hypothesis to Theorem 1.4, namely "if x ∈ S(ρ̄) and ρ̄|G_x is reducible, then ρ̄^{I_x} ≠ 0", so the statement matches what §3 proves. Other fixes also work but take more effort:
- Keep the statement general and define R^min in the Diamond sense, i.e. ρ(I_x) ≅ ρ̄(I_x) at such x, as in Cor. 1.5(1). The Hecke side then needs a new type-cutting bundle at those x, e.g. U_x = K_0(x^{max(a1,a2)}) with the character ψ̃1(a)ψ̃2(d).
- State the Hecke side for the twist ρ̄⊗χ̄, with N, X_U, T and m taken from the twist.
Corollaries 1.5 and 1.6 then each need a one-line twisting reduction, which is valid: weight-one modularity, finite image, the minimality in Cor. 1.5(1) and R^min are all unchanged by twisting by the Teichmüller lift of a character unramified at p.
sourceIssues.reason:
I checked the page images at pp. 303, 310–311, 338, 340 and 342 against the text. The same wording is in arXiv v2.

(1) Theorem 1.4 as printed covers every odd irreducible ρ̄ that is unramified at p. The whole proof runs under the §3.1 standing assumption. §3.8 (p. 340) says "We now deduce Theorem 1.4, under Assumption 3.9 … we take X_U = X = X_1(N)/H". §3.9.2 (p. 342, and p. 354) removes only Assumption 3.9, the vexing primes. The §3.1 assumption is never removed; the only thing said about it is the one-line twisting remark.

(2) For ρ̄|G_x ≅ ψ̄1⊕ψ̄2 with both characters ramified, ρ̄^{I_x} = 0. So Definition 3.1(4) already fails for ρ̄ over k, and the functor is empty. The R^min of the introduction then has to mean Diamond-minimal (ρ(I_x) ≅ ρ̄(I_x); compare Corollary 1.5(1)), and the §3 machinery does not apply to it directly.

(3) On the Galois side, twisting by the Teichmüller lift of χ̄ does give R^min(ρ̄) ≅ R^min(ρ̄⊗χ̄). The determinant condition and the inertia condition both carry over. On the Hecke side, the Serre level drops at x (from x² to x or 1), and X_U changes with it. The Hecke algebra of ρ̄' = ρ̄⊗χ̄ has no maximal ideal for ρ̄: ρ̄ cannot occur at level N' < N. So the twist does not directly give "X_U a quotient of X_1(N), m corresponding to ρ̄".

(4) Taking the paper's own level structure directly does not work either. For P(ρ̄) (p. 342) the paper uses U_x = {g ≡ (∗ ∗; 0 d) mod x^{c_x}, d of p-power order}, which here has c_x = 2. Take x ≡ 1 mod p and θ a nontrivial character of Z_x^× of p-power order and conductor x. The representation π(ψ̃1θ, ψ̃2θ^{-1}) has conductor 1+1 = 2 and central character ψ̃1ψ̃2, which is trivial on elements d of p-power order. Its newvector is therefore U_x-invariant, it is congruent to ρ̄, and it is non-minimal. Under the §3.1 assumption, by contrast, ψ̄1 is unramified, and such twists raise the conductor to 1+c_x, which excludes them. So the assumption is really used.

Conclusion: the statement of Theorem 1.4 goes beyond what is proved. The theorem is probably still true with a different choice of X_U and L_σ, so this is a gap, not an error. It is minor, and the fix is routine.

Dependencies: Corollaries 1.5 and 1.6 are unchanged by twisting, so they survive. §4 assumes minimal conductor among twists (p. 351), which implies the §3.1 condition. Only Theorem 1.4's generality is affected. Defences I tried, and why each fails. I checked page images for pp. 303, 310, 311, 340 and 342 and read the text of pp. 325–330 and 350–354.

(1) "R^min refers to §3, so the §3.1 assumption is implicit." Theorem 1.4 lists its hypotheses explicitly: p ≥ 3, odd, irreducible (which gives absolute irreducibility for p odd), and unramified at p. These are all the §3.1 standing assumptions except the twist condition. Under the paper's own Def. 3.1(4), a ρ̄ with ρ̄|G_x ≅ ψ̄1⊕ψ̄2, both characters ramified, has ρ̄^{I_x} = 0. No lift then satisfies (4), so the functor is empty and "R^min" means nothing. The intro must therefore intend Diamond-minimality, which is the reading of Cor. 1.5(1): "ρ(I_v) ≅ ρ̄(I_v) or dim ρ^{I_v} = dim ρ̄^{I_v} = 1". The §3 proof never treats that notion.

(2) "By twisting, WLOG." On the Galois side this works. There is a global χ̄ with χ̄|I_x = ψ̄1^{-1}, ramified only at such x, and R^min(ρ̄) ≅ R^min(ρ̄⊗χ̄). On the Hecke side it does not. The twist has a smaller Serre level N' (the x-part drops from x^{a1+a2} to x^{cond(ψ̄2/ψ̄1)}), and its m' corresponds to ρ̄⊗χ̄. Theorem 1.4 requires m to correspond to ρ̄ itself, and ρ̄ does not occur at level N'. The paper says nothing beyond the one-line remark on p. 310, which is the only occurrence of "twist" in §3 apart from the remark on p. 334 about twisting a scalar local ρ̄ to trivial.

(3) "The paper's own X_U works anyway." It does not in general. §3.3 (p. 325) takes X = X_1(N)/H with H the p-part of (Z/N)^×, and §3.9 (p. 342) takes U_x = {g ≡ (* *; 0 d) mod x^{c_x}, d of p-power order} for x ∈ P(ρ̄). Suppose x ≡ 1 mod p and θ is a p-power-order character of Z_x^× of conductor x. Then π(ψ̃1θ, ψ̃2θ^{-1}) has conductor exponent a1+a2 = c_x, because ψ̃iθ^{±1} is still ramified with the same conductor. Its central character ψ̃1ψ̃2 has prime-to-p order, so it is trivial on p-power d, and the newvector is U_x-invariant. This representation is congruent to ρ̄ but not minimal. So Theorem 3.14 ("follows from the choice of N and H") and the p. 341 claim "all minimal lifts … appear in H^0(X_U, ω)" do not give R^min → T_m. Under the §3.1 assumption, ψ̄1 is unramified and such twists raise the conductor, so the assumption is really used. A concrete case exists: p = 3, x = 13, ρ̄|I_x ≅ χ̄ ⊕ χ̄^{-1} with χ̄ of order 4.

(4) Where the proof ends. §3.8 deduces Theorem 1.4 "under Assumption 3.9", and §3.9.2 removes only that assumption (vexing primes). The §3.1 assumption is never removed.

Consequences:
- Only the generality of Theorem 1.4 is affected. The theorem is very likely true with a type-cutting L_σ built with the paper's own §3.9 formalism, so this is a gap rather than a false statement.
- Cor. 1.5 and 1.6 ("immediately deduce") still hold after a routine twist.
- §4 assumes minimal conductor among twists (p. 361), which implies the condition, so it is unaffected.
- The proposed correction (add the hypothesis) is right and minimal.
- A side observation, not part of this candidate: p. 340's "if x^2|N, then U_x = 0" fits the both-ramified case but misses a wildly ramified ψ̄2 under the §3.1 assumption. U_x ∈ T_m still follows from the invariant-line argument in that case.
